subject: Renewal options and fiscal alignment for BrightWave capacity
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: John L. Carter <john.carter@brightwave.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal options and fiscal alignment for BrightWave capacity

Hi John —

Thanks again for the chat this morning. Per our conversation I pulled together three pragmatic options that balance cost, predictability and the flexibility you asked for. High level: we can support co-terming into your Oct 1 fiscal boundary, offer structured ramps, and provide soft auto-renew opt-outs if you want more runway. Details below — happy to jump on a quick 20-min follow-up with procurement/legal.

Option A — 12-month (pay-as-you-go + auto-renew):
- Standard hosted pricing, no prepay; native autoscaling.
- Auto-renew by default with 30-day written opt-out.
- Best if you want minimal ops commitments; higher unit price.

Option B — 18-month hybrid commit (recommended):
- 18 months total, with a front-loaded partial prepay for first 6 months to cover ramp (we typically do 40–60% of expected first-year runrate).
- Ramp schedule: Milestone credits at month 3 and month 9 tied to onboarding KPIs (latency <125ms p50, successful prefix cache hits).
- Pricing: modest blended discount vs A; includes one planned model-variant fall back.
- Co-term to Oct 1, 2028 possible via prorated credit for remaining months.

Option C — 24-month committed (multi-year, capacity guarantee):
- Greater discount, predictable seats/throughput, SLA crediting, and capacity reservations for burst windows.
- Quarterly true-up with floor/ceiling protections.

Attachments: BrightWave_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_proposal_v1.xlsx (detailed numbers).

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm whether procurement wants co-term to Oct 1 2028; 2) tell me target discount / prepay appetite; 3) if yes to B/C, I’ll send a draft with the ramp milestones and a proposed DocuSign link for signatures.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer

Appreciate this level of detail. A few asks from our side so we can move this through procurement and legal quickly:

- BrightWave’s fiscal year runs Oct 1 — could we align the contract to co-term on Oct 1, 2028? Preferably a clean co-term rather than a mid-quarter renewal.
- We like the look of Option B (18-month hybrid). Can you confirm whether the partial prepay counts toward committed consumption for true-up? We want to avoid double-billing on an annual true-up.
- For legal: will you accept a soft auto-renew opt-out (30 days notice) instead of hard auto-renew?
- Procurement also asked if we can frontload credits for the onboarding phase and whether there’s a proration mechanism if we co-term early.

Looping in procurement@brightwave.ai and legal (they’ll want a redline). If you can provide a version that maps to Oct 1 co-term and explicitly calls out how prepay interacts with true-up, that’ll speed this along.

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick take from GTM and operations perspective:

1) Pricing band: For an 18-month hybrid (40% front-load prepay) we can sit at a mid-band discount of ~6–8% off list relative to pay-as-you-go. That aligns comps and keeps margin while making the economics material for the customer.

2) Prepay vs true-up: Finance is OK with applying the prepay toward committed consumption on the first rolling true-up period, provided we include explicit language that any unused prepay at co-term converts to credits that may be applied against the last billing period (prorated). We do NOT want to expose cash refunds.

3) Co-term mechanics & proration: We can co-term to Oct 1, 2028. Recommend structure: set an 18-month contractual term that starts on signature date but includes a co-term clause: if customer elects Oct 1 co-term, we apply a prorated credit for the months between signature and Oct 1 to the committed bucket. That keeps accounting clean and is an easy operational lift.

4) Ramp milestones (ops & CS): Neha — can you confirm the onboarding KPIs below are realistic?
- Month 1: baseline integration and test traffic (health checks green)
- Month 3: 80% of peak traffic routed through Redwood with latency & correctness KPIs met
- Month 9: steady-state performance; KV hit rate >70% for prefixes targeted for cache

Neha: if OK, we’ll include milestone credit schedule: 10% credit at month 3, 10% at month 9 (applied to committed consumption bucket).

5) Legal tolerance: Marissa — are you okay with soft auto-renew opt-out (30 days)? I recommend yes for a strategic customer — it reduces friction.

I’ve attached a quick redline suggestion to pricing_proposal_v1.xlsx and will produce a SOW snippet for the co-term/proration clause.

Camila Reyes

- Ramp milestones & credits: 10% credit applied at month 3 (integration milestone), 10% at month 9 (steady state). Milestones tied to KPIs documented in the SOW.
- Auto-renew: Soft auto-renew with 30-day written opt-out.
